notes:
> Note: 0.6.26 was prepared but never tagged, so this release also delivers everything listed under the 0.6.26 section below — none of it has reached users before this build.


Structural editor fixes that stop Backspace, Tab and bracket-typing from damaging your text; a journal calendar that scrolls the stream instead of leaving it; live sync that survives a reconnect; and in-app feedback on iOS (dev channel).

**New**

- **Send feedback from inside the app.** iOS gains a real way to report a bug —
  **Settings → About → Send feedback**, findable from Settings search and the
  global search surface, or just **shake the device**. The form is a message, a
  type, an optional email, and an opt-in "include recent logs"; the shake is
  ignored in an unprovisioned build, over an open form, and while you're typing
  in the editor, so iOS's own shake-to-undo still belongs to the writer. Before
  this, a TestFlight tester had no in-app way to say anything at all. Desktop's
  Cmd+K **Send Feedback** is unchanged and now pinned by a test so a refactor
  can't quietly drop it. (PRD Addendum 14 §N2; `mobile_shake_feedback` kill
  switch; #704/#758.)

**Fixes & polish**

- **Live sync no longer goes quiet after a reconnect** — a device could land on
  a discarded server channel and silently receive no updates until the app was
  restarted, falling back to the 15-minute refresh. (Addendum 31 §AB; #750.)
- **Backspace and Delete stop damaging structure.** Backspace on a lone nested
  bullet used to re-parent the whole list — and because that corruption
  persisted, it synced to every device. Backspace or Delete at a heading no
  longer orphans its children to the root; Backspace no longer merges your text
  into a *hidden* collapsed block, where it simply looked deleted. (PRD Addendum
  2 §B+D, §B5; Fixes #685; #690.)
- **Text stops falling into code blocks.** Backspace or Delete against a code
  fence used to silently append your prose *inside* the fence, or delete the
  fence outright. The new rule: the caret crosses the fence, the text never
  does. (#690.)
- **Tab commits the highlighted suggestion in a picker.** In the `[[note]]`,
  `#tag` and `((block))` pickers, Tab used to quietly re-parent your block and
  leave the popup open; Shift+Tab used to mint a link when you were only
  reaching for un-indent. (PRD Addendum 1 §A9.1; #689.)
- **Enter under an empty picker is no longer destructive.** Typing `((zzzzzz`,
  getting "No block matches" and pressing Enter used to split your block under a
  visible popup and strand the auto-paired `))` on the new line. It now just
  dismisses. (#689.)
- **Selecting across a link and typing a bracket no longer destroys the link.**
  Wrapping a selection that contains a `[[wikilink]]` or `#tag` used to delete
  it; the link and the surrounding formatting now survive. (#689.)
- **Bullet nesting stops at eight levels everywhere.** A ninth Tab used to draw
  a tenth nested list while the stored depth clamped at eight — the structure on
  screen and the hierarchy in the database disagreeing. (PRD Addendum 2 §B9.5;
  #689.)
- **The slash menu stays out of places it doesn't belong** — inside a code
  block, and inside a half-typed `[[…]]` or `((…))`, where it used to stack two
  live pickers over the same text and could produce a wikilink titled `foo /`.
  (PRD Addendum 1 §A9.4; #689.)
- **Three typed backticks no longer leave a run of backticks inside the new code
  block.** (#689.)
- **Your last keystrokes survive the page going away.** A reload, the window
  hiding, or focus leaving the webview could drop the edits that hadn't been
  saved yet — desktop returned an empty paragraph where mobile returned the
  text. Desktop now flushes pending saves on all three. (#688.)
- **Picking a date from the journal's own calendar scrolls the journal to that
  day** instead of replacing the stream with a single-day note view. A ⌘- or
  ⇧-click, and a pick from Home, the week ribbon or a note, still open the day
  as before; clicking a greyed-out overflow cell now moves the calendar to that
  month. (PRD Addendum 1 §A10.5; Fixes #682/#683; #754.)
- **A daily note dated in the future no longer mis-anchors the journal.** It
  sorted above today and took the first slot, which threw off where the journal
  opened, where "jump to today" went, and made the day list reload on every
  Journal click. (PRD Addendum 5 §E2.7; #754.)

**Mobile (iOS, dev channel — not in this build)**

Most of the work since 0.6.26 was the iPhone/iPad app, which ships only on the
dev channel and is not part of this DMG. Recorded so the notes are honest about
where the effort went:

- **⌘Z undoes what you just typed on iPad.** With autocorrect on, the word you
  are in the middle of *is* a live composition, so a ⌘ chord pressed right after
  typing — exactly when you reach for one — was swallowed. Undo/redo on the
  EditBar were dead in the same moment. (PRD Addendum 27; #688.)
- **An unbound chord no longer types a letter into your note.** ⌘K used to
  insert a stray `k` and ⌘⇧. a stray `.` — the chord dead *and* the note
  corrupted. ⌘⇧. now reaches Collapse, and hardware **⌘K opens search** from a
  focused editor. (#688; #691/#749/#762.)
- **The EditBar's `#` and `[[` buttons work after a word.** `#` used to insert a
  dead character that opened no picker — a silent failure, because the character
  appeared — and `[[` glued the chip onto the word before it. (PRD Addendum 36
  §10 — "tapping ≡ typing"; #688.)
- **The iPhone's on-screen Delete key runs the same logic as a hardware
  keyboard.** It never reached the editor's keymap, so bullets merged into one
  list item and children were never re-homed. (#690.)
- **Journal "Today" really goes to today**, and a tap in a day's side gutter
  puts the caret in *that* day — every gutter tap in the stream used to land in
  the oldest day on screen. Tapping a day heading or ticking a todo no longer
  raises the keyboard. (PRD Addendum 5 §E2.10; Fixes #695/#702/#717; #743.)
- **The docked References pencil no longer crashes the app** on iPad — the one
  shared webview was being re-parented from inside SwiftUI's own layout pass.
  And **renaming a note now shows everywhere**: the rename always reached the
  database, but the iPad sidebar's Recents and Pinned kept the old name until
  you quit. (PRD Addendum 36 §15; Fixes #693; #744.)
- **Deleting or archiving a note removes it from the list you're looking at.**
  It used to survive on screen for at least eight seconds with the database
  already correct. (#745.)
- **Folders, Tags, Todos, Bookmarks and Trash are reachable on iPhone** — they
  were drawn with a chevron but disabled, which meant a trashed note could not
  be restored on a phone at all. (PRD Addendum 32 §4; #745.)
- **Recents is ordered by when you last opened a note**, not last edited,
  matching Cmd+K's Continue list; opening a journal day from Recents or search
  lands on the journal stream rather than a bare day page; and the **Start page**
  setting now does something on iOS. (PRD Addendum 22 §6.4, Addendum 29 §Z6;
  #745.)
- **The iPad tab strip scrolls.** Tabs used to overflow *underneath* the new-tab,
  calendar and References buttons, leaving the active tab's close button
  unreachable; the active tab is now kept in view. The tab rail on iPhone scrolls
  the active card into view too. (PRD Addendum 33 §3.1; #745/#747.)
- **The Todos page's checkboxes actually tick.** They were decoration — tapping
  one opened the note, and the function that would have written the change had no
  caller anywhere in the shell. (#747.)
- **The caret lands where you tap in a note title**, instead of snapping to a
  word boundary or to the start when you tap past a short title. (#747.)
- **The iPhone's top bar gets out of the way when you scroll** — the collapse
  logic was correct and had never once run, because the shell was watching the
  wrong scroller. (PRD Addendum 32; #747.)
- **A failed sign-in shows real copy.** It used to print the raw transport error
  verbatim; it now says whether you're offline, the server is unreachable, the
  request timed out or the connection is insecure — and only the category is
  logged. (Privacy Invariant; #747.)
- **Settings are findable from search**, in path form (`Appearance → Theme`),
  opening Settings at that pane with the row flashed. (PRD Addendum 33 §2.4;
  #747.)
- **Long-press a link in your text to open its references** — the sheet on
  iPhone, the docked panel on iPad. It's the summon that doesn't make you leave
  the sentence you're reading. (PRD Addendum 33 §4.3; Fixes #706; #743/#748.)
- **Search finds a journal day by name on iPhone** — "aug 5", "yesterday",
  "5/8". Before, `aug 5` returned August 15th and 25th by title substring and
  offered to create a note called "aug 5"; the only real route was about a dozen
  flicks of scrolling per five weeks back. A **Dates** section now sits nearest
  the field, and activating a row creates and opens that day in the journal
  stream. (PRD Addendum 29 §Z8; Fixes #699; #743/#748.)
- **The EditBar survives summoning a reference card on iPad.** A long-press
  opens iPadOS's own context menu, which takes the keyboard off screen for as
  long as you read it — and the bar was never put back for the rest of the
  session. (PRD Addendum 36 §15; Fixes #698; #755.)
- **Pinned notes have somewhere to show on iPhone.** Pinning wrote, listed and
  refreshed, but only the iPad sidebar rendered a group — a write with no reader,
  which is worse than an absent feature, because the app confirms an action it
  then never shows. The phone landing gains the same group, the same shared
  manual order and a "Show all" row into a real Pinned page; a pinned journal day
  can now be unpinned. (PRD Addendum 22 §6.2; Fixes #713; #759.)
- **Archive is in Organise on both families** — an archived note used to be
  listed nowhere. Archive rows offer Unarchive and Delete, where Delete trashes
  rather than destroying, so it doesn't become the one unrecoverable delete in
  the shell. (Fixes #681/#696; #759.)
- **The open note's actions are back on the iPad tab strip**, in the `⋯` beside
  the References toggle — a note that is neither pinned nor in Recents has no row
  on screen while you're reading it. (PRD Addendum 33; #759.)
- **A remotely disabled References surface now behaves as if the feature never
  existed.** With the switch off, the bundle still claimed the long-press and
  swallowed the follow-up tap while the shell refused it, so the user
  long-pressed a link and got nothing, having spent a tap that would otherwise
  have navigated. A new capability handshake means nothing is bound at all when a
  surface is off, and a remote flip now takes effect mid-session. (Fixes #749;
  #762.)
- **The Infiniti Pro preview is visible on iPhone and iPad (dev channel).** The
  Pro section, plan picker and Pro's route into the recovery-key ceremony had
  been built but dark on every channel — the flag that reveals them was never
  published. It is now on for dev. Nothing is for sale: the entitlement is a
  stub and there is no StoreKit in this arc. (PRD Addendum 35 §MS-9;
  `mobile_pro_preview`; #703.)

**Under the hood**

- **Two standing audits, 1,021 falsifiable rows.** The **editor-parity audit**
  wrote a **597-row** desktop editor contract (453 rows pinned to a
  `file:line`), recorded a WebKit oracle with a Chromium control, then replayed
  all 597 rows against the mobile bundle, 106 against a real iPhone simulator and
  76 against an iPad's hardware-chord surface — producing a ranked iOS gap report
  and, incidentally, 23 *desktop* bug candidates (6 HIGH). The **iOS usage
  audit** catalogued **424 rows** across Family M and Family D against a
  deterministic 101-note / 1,337-block vault seeded through the real storage
  write boundary, and de-duplicated the results into 50 ranked issues (2 P0, 6
  P1). Neither audit changed a line of product code by design — every fix in
  this release descends from them. (`docs/editor-parity/`,
  `docs/ios-usage-audit/`, `crates/audit-fixture/`; #686/#692/#753.)
- **~200 new regression tests** across the fix wave that followed — roughly 92
  iOS unit/XCUITest rows, 71 frontend vitest/Playwright rows and 38 Rust rows —
  each pinned at the layer the rule actually lives in, and the structural ones
  verified to fail on the pre-fix source before they were accepted.
- **A new house rule: audit findings go to GitHub Issues before the arc
  closes.** The usage audit produced 50 findings and no tracker — the same shape
  earlier bug hunts took. A finding that lives only in a markdown table is a
  finding nobody picks up, so one issue per distinct root cause, severity and
  platform in the title, cross-linked both ways, is now non-negotiable in
  `CLAUDE.md`. 49 issues were filed against this arc. (#742.)
- **And a testing rule the audit paid for.** BC-10 — the Backspace hierarchy
  shift — wrote a *self-referential* `parent_id` and replicated it through sync
  while a pinned unit test and both e2e engines stayed green, because the node
  tree alone was correct throughout. Any row whose action moves a block between
  parents must now assert `parentId`/`depth`, not just the structure on screen.
  (`docs/editor-parity/README.md`; #753.)
- **The realtime reconnect bug was two server bugs.** The fan-out registry looked
  a vault's channel up, released its lock, and only then reserved a subscriber
  slot — so a departing socket's cleanup landing in that window evicted a channel
  a live socket was already committed to, and that socket's nudges went nowhere
  for its whole life. Adversarial review then found a second: the connection slot
  and device record were reserved before the WebSocket upgrade, but axum only
  runs the upgrade callback on success, so a client vanishing in between leaked
  both permanently — past the cap an account sticks at 429 for the life of the
  process, and a departed device reads as connected, suppressing its silent
  pushes. Both are now held by RAII guards released on drop. (PRD Addendum 31
  §AB; **Postmortem-0010**; Fixes #750; #763.)
- **A deterministic virtual clock for the sync simulator**, so the realtime
  reconnect-storm scenario stops depending on wall-clock timing — it advances to
  the nearest waiter rather than waiting, cutting that scenario's ceiling from
  167s to 110s. Nothing installs a clock in a shipped build. (**ADR-0022**;
  #763.)
- **A known residual, stated honestly:** the sync engine now reports when a cycle
  was skipped because one was already in flight, but the shipped desktop and
  mobile hosts still discard that flag — so a manual "Sync now" can still
  silently do nothing. Tracked as #756.
- **The feedback pipeline is now one shared crate.** The §N2 payload, the log
  sanitizer and the Worker POST moved into a Tauri-free `crates/feedback` used by
  both shells, so the desktop and iOS paths cannot silently diverge; a Worker
  rejection shows static copy instead of a raw status code. (#758.)
- **CI robustness.** The per-worktree e2e port derivation now skips Chromium's
  restricted ports — a worktree that hashed onto one made every e2e spec fail at
  once as `ERR_UNSAFE_PORT`, which read as a catastrophic product regression
  (#751). The block-write linearity pin was re-estimated so it stops flaking
  under runner load (#752). The E2E smoke cap moved 90 → 150 minutes because
  healthy, fully-passing runs were being killed by our own timeout (#746) — a
  stopgap, superseded by the approved sharding/path-filter work. And the docs
  site built red before the parity corrections landed: unescaped pipes inside
  inline-code spans split GFM table cells and exposed a literal `{{…}}` that
  VitePress tokenized as an interpolation (#753).
